body_es: Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) es el servicio de cómputo fundamental de AWS, que permite lanzar servidores virtuales llamados instancias en minutos. Las instancias se agrupan en familias según su caso de uso: propósito general (t3, m6i), optimizadas para cómputo (c6i, c7g), optimizadas para memoria (r6i, x2idn), aceleradas (p4, g5, inf2) y optimizadas para almacenamiento (i3, d3). Las instancias t3/t4g usan créditos de CPU para ráfagas temporales de rendimiento, siendo ideales para cargas de trabajo variables. Para el examen SAA-C03 es clave entender los modelos de precios: bajo demanda (sin compromiso), instancias reservadas (descuento hasta 72% con 1 o 3 años de compromiso), Savings Plans (flexibilidad entre familias), Spot (hasta 90% de descuento, interrumpibles) y hosts dedicados. La elección correcta del tipo de instancia impacta directamente en costos y rendimiento. EC2 soporta placement groups para controlar la ubicación física: cluster (baja latencia), spread (alta disponibilidad) y partition (grandes clusters distribuidos). Los Storage Groups y las AMIs permiten reutilizar configuraciones de instancias de forma eficiente. Desde dentro de la instancia, el EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) expone datos sobre ella misma —zona de disponibilidad, ID de instancia— y, si hay un rol IAM asociado, credenciales temporales bajo `iam/security-credentials/{{rol}}`; no da métricas de rendimiento (eso es CloudWatch) ni lanza instancias.
body_en: Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) is AWS's core compute service, allowing you to provision virtual machines called instances in minutes. Instance families are tailored to specific workload profiles: general purpose (t3, m6i, m7g), compute-optimized (c6i, c7g), memory-optimized (r6i, x2idn), accelerated computing (p4, g5, inf2), and storage-optimized (i3, d3). T-series instances use CPU credits to burst above baseline, making them cost-effective for variable or low-average workloads. Understanding pricing models is essential for the SAA-C03 exam: On-Demand (pay per second, no commitment), Reserved Instances (up to 72% discount with 1 or 3-year terms), Savings Plans (flexible commitment across families), Spot Instances (up to 90% off but interruptible), and Dedicated Hosts (physical server allocation for licensing compliance). EC2 placement groups control physical placement: Cluster groups tightly pack instances for low-latency networking, Spread groups distribute across distinct hardware to reduce correlated failures, and Partition groups separate large-scale distributed systems. Instance metadata, user data scripts, and AMIs allow repeatable, automated instance configuration at scale. From inside the instance, the EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) exposes data about the instance itself — availability zone, instance ID — and, when an IAM role is attached, temporary credentials under `iam/security-credentials/{{role}}`; it does not provide performance metrics (that's CloudWatch) and it cannot launch instances.
example_code:
# Launch an EC2 instance
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --image-id ami-0abcdef1234567890 \
  --instance-type t3.micro \
  --key-name my-key-pair \
  --security-group-ids sg-903004f8 \
  --subnet-id subnet-6e7f829e \
  --count 1

# List instances
aws ec2 describe-instances --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,InstanceType,State.Name]'
